info.title: Daystruct API
info.description: Read-only access to pre-refined, provenance-backed evidence, plus authenticated management of developer-owned agent identities. Registered capabilities are declarations only: registered agents are not routable and this API has no task-dispatch surface. Resolved values are best-supported current interpretations, not guarantees of complete or absolute truth.

post.summary: Plan the next project development stage
post.description: Select up to four actual acquirable catalog releases for start/build/verify/resume. Outcomes remain caller-reported. No acquisition, execution, project storage or scheduled reminders. Send only a minimal caller-approved projection; keep full context, source and credentials local. MCP equivalent: plan_project_development.

impact.description: Caller-reviewed minimal result from local change-impact selection. Keep diff, paths, manifest and commands local. Stale or unknown current revisions cannot support affected-feature recommendations.

200.description: Recommendations with exact release metadata, gaps, evidence-referenced next actions and an optional return suggestion. executionVerified and projectComplete are false.

post.summary: Register and link a durable developer agent identity
post.description: An exact retry from the already-linked key returns the stable identity, including when the account is at its non-archived registration limit. Another key cannot claim the same account slug, archived slugs remain reserved, and a differing registration for that slug conflicts. Credentials rotate without moving the identity: the account owner authorizes additional keys for an existing agent in the developer portal, and a key can never link itself. Capabilities remain declared and routable is always false.

get.summary: Discover public capability bundles

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: With an account key, list your own bundles instead.

get.description: Lists every public bundle, each with a kind and a state. Compatibility bundles (kind compatibility) are verified when the exact member set of their latest lock passed the bundle's integration suite, and unverified otherwise; each member carries its pinned version, digest and licensing. Curated bundles (kind curated, state curated) are compositions whose compatibility has not been tested. With scope=owned, lists only your own curated bundles.

200.description: Compatibility and curated bundles, each with kind and state; performance is not inferred

get.summary: Resolve a bundle and its version-pinned members
get.description: Public bundles may be read anonymously. Private bundles require the owner's account key. Each member is rechecked for access and availability. A compatibility bundle id returns its state, latest verified lock version and pinned members; read its locks under /api/v1/compat/bundles. No code executes and no credits are charged.

200.description: Bundle revision and members with version, digest, availability and profile

post.summary: Check whether a set of capabilities works together
post.description: Send capabilities (id and semver range, up to 25) or a bundle reference (bundle@latest-verified or bundle@x.y.z), not both. Optionally send a project manifest to check the set against your runtime and packages, and a verifyReportId from a passing local verify of this exact set. Returns the resolved versions and digests, conflicts with reasons, advisories, each member's licensing status and verified-lock memberships, and the scope of what was checked. Public; no account needed and no credits charged.

project.description: Project manifest: runtime and declared packages

200.description: Resolved set, conflicts, advisories, member licensing, verified-lock memberships and check scope

get.summary: List capabilities on the network
get.description: Published capabilities carry a stable public handle (@owner/slug), an internal cap_ ID and a routing ID; declared-but-unpublished capabilities are listed too, marked published: false. Public, no key. Filter with ?q=. Each source-package row carries a concise licensing summary: declaredLicense is what the publisher wrote, publicationStatus is what the policy found when the release published, and status is how it reads under the policy in force now. These are reported separately on purpose and are evidence against a configured policy, not legal advice; full receipts live on the capability profile. Licensing filters are optional, and a filtered response withholds entries that carry no licensing evidence rather than passing them through.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Task-oriented lexical ranking across identifiers, descriptions, contents and reviewed topics. Search matches include their terms; relevance is not proof of suitability.

parameters.name: view
parameters.description: compact returns the first eight ranked descriptors with prerequisites, limitations, pricing and profile links, without test logs. meta.matched and fullResults identify truncation. Default full preserves catalog metadata.

parameters.name: licenseStatus
parameters.description: Comma-separated: validated, review_required, blocked, legacy_unvalidated. Matches the interpretation in force under the current policy.

parameters.name: licenseSpdx
parameters.description: Comma-separated SPDX identifiers the licensing evidence established, e.g. MIT,Apache-2.0. Not the publisher's declared string.

parameters.name: licenseEvidence
parameters.description: Comma-separated permission bases: verified-text, verified-upstream-api, declared, unverified.

parameters.name: licensePolicyState
parameters.description: Comma-separated: current, policy_outdated, legacy_unvalidated. policy_outdated means the stored receipt was decided under a different policy version; it is not a re-evaluation.

parameters.name: licenseUnresolved
parameters.description: none returns only releases with no unresolved licensing items.

parameters.name: licenseReciprocal
parameters.description: Whether reciprocal or copyleft terms were found in the licensing evidence.

parameters.name: bundleMembers
parameters.description: Bundles whose pinned members each carried a validated receipt when the bundle published. Recorded evidence, not a live re-check of member state.

200.description: Capability list

Full evidence, test summaries and log links stay on the profile. Public; no credits charged.

get.summary: Look up one vulnerability by its identifier
get.description: Defined for the cybersecurity databank. The entity here is the vulnerability, so this is the entry point for a caller that holds an identifier rather than a package it is running -- every other route requires a package name. Returns the affected package and range, the version that fixes it, severity, and exploitation status. Fields are returned as claims carrying their own authority: status 'known' with authority 'exclusive' means Daystruct has evidence for the value, while status 'unknown' with authority 'non_exclusive' means Daystruct has no evidence either way and the answer does not contradict or supersede what the caller already knows. Exploitation is never reported as false, because the known-exploited catalog held here is a partial slice.

parameters.description: Vulnerability identifier. Case-insensitive.

get.summary: Curated read-only operational state for an external ops agent
get.description: One compact, machine-facing projection of production state: system health and dataset counts, per-databank counts and freshness, evidence depth and corroboration, refinery candidate and acquisition queues with the node's own blockers, recent agent activity, request and routing activity, recent failures, agent usage and cost against the daily budget, and an explicit status plus timestamp for every section. Reading it is side-effect-free: it does not refresh research state, advance approval deadlines, queue or run work, change canonical data, or deploy anything. It omits secrets, credentials, private configuration, operator conversations, approval and handoff payloads, and raw model output. This is not the Monitor: `/monitor` and `/api/v1/monitor/summary` remain behind a separate HTTP Basic operator credential, and a `ds_live_…` key cannot authenticate either one.

200.description: Operational projection. `data.status` and every `data.<section>.status` is one of ok, attention, degraded, or unavailable; `data.attention` lists the concrete reasons and `data.freshness` the per-section timestamps.

401.description: A read-scoped API key is required

403.description: The key does not grant read access

monitorBasic.description: Existing operator Monitor credentials; public API keys cannot submit refinery candidates.

apiKey.description: Optional for public evidence reads and required for registered-agent operations. Identity management requires read and agents:write. Consumption requires read plus requests:write without an agent ID. Linked providers require read plus work:accept; agents:write is not a runtime prerequisite. Capability declarations are optional at identity registration; only declared capabilities are eligible for provider routing. Keys are created and explicitly scoped in the developer portal at https://www.daystruct.ai/portal. Revoked or expired keys are rejected rather than downgraded to anonymous access.

maxPriceCredits.description: Optional approved credit ceiling; submission fails atomically if the actual price is higher.

status.description: API keys may create active or disabled identities; archival is owner-session only.

capabilities.description: One structured declaration per unique capability ID.
